chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Basir said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who trimmed one of his fingernails while he was in the state of Ihram. He said: Upon him is, for every nail, the value of a Mudd of food, until it reaches ten. If he trimmed the nails of both his hands entirely, then upon him is the blood of a sheep. I said: If he trimmed the nails of both his feet and hands entirely? He said: If he did that in one sitting, then upon him is one blood (of a sheep). And if he did it separately in two sittings, then upon him are two bloods (of sheep).

key_terms.إحرام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.دم: Blood, referring to the sacrifice of a sheep
key_terms.مد: A unit of volume measurement for food

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for trimming nails while in the state of Ihram during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahar establishes the specific fidya for trimming nails while in Ihram, distinguishing between individual nail penalties and the collective expiation of a sheep for all hand nails. It further clarifies that performing the act in separate sessions incurs double the penalty, reflecting the juristic principle that distinct actions in distinct times constitute separate obligations. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for understanding the granularity of Ihram violations and their corresponding compensations.
